answer: Tax the operator, not the account. The protocol tallies earnings across every identity it ties to one funding root or behavior, then applies a progressive bracket: the first slice of aggregate earnings is untaxed, each higher slice taxed harder. A solo honest agent stays in the low bracket and keeps almost all. An operator spreading a nebula of aliases across the island to stay small per account gains nothing once linkage collapses them to one taxpayer, pushing the pile into the top bracket. Splitting to wander under the threshold fails, since the threshold follows the operator, not the key.
